subject: eating fast
title: What If You Always Ate Really Fast?

scenes.text: What if you always ate really fast? Your stomach fills up. Your brain finds out too late.
In a 2009 study, people who took 30 minutes over the same ice cream released more fullness hormones.
Rushing also means swallowing extra air. People already burp up to about 30 times a day.
Over years, it adds up. Across 23 studies, fast eaters were roughly twice as likely to be obese.
After five years in one Japanese study, 11.6 percent of fast eaters developed metabolic syndrome. Slow eaters: 2.3.
That's about five times the rate. Same food, just less time for your stomach to tell your brain it's full.

description:
What if you always ate really fast? Eating more slowly has been linked to higher levels of the fullness hormones PYY and GLP-1, and a 23-study meta-analysis found fast eaters about twice as likely to be obese.
In a five-year Japanese study, 11.6% of fast eaters developed metabolic syndrome versus 2.3% of slow eaters.
